Cushion springs
short coil springs or rubber blocks between the primary driven gear and the clutch basket that let the gear turn a few degrees relative to the basket, absorbing firing pulses and shift shocks.
Scissors gear
a gear split into two halves, one spring-loaded against the other, so that backlash with the mating gear is taken up and gear rattle at idle is avoided.
Mean friction radius
the radius at which the friction of a clutch or brake lining can be taken to act; for a bedded-in lining, about the mean of its inner and outer radii.
Slip torque
the torque at which a clutch begins to slip, equal to friction coefficient times spring force times mean friction radius times number of friction faces.
JASO MA
a Japanese standard for four-stroke motorcycle oils tested for wet-clutch friction; MA2 is the higher-friction grade. JASO MB oils are for dry-clutch scooters.
Primary kickstart
a kickstart that drives the clutch basket directly, so the engine can be started in any gear with the clutch lever pulled.
Overall ratio
the product of the primary, gear and final drive ratios: the total reduction from crankshaft to rear wheel in a given gear.
Rolling circumference
the distance a tyre travels in one turn under load, about 3 % less than its geometric circumference.
Gear step
the ratio between adjacent gear ratios, which sets how far engine speed falls on each upshift.
Overdrive top gear
a top gear so tall that the engine cannot reach its power peak in it, chosen for lower cruising rpm, noise and fuel use.
Positive Neutral Finder
Kawasaki's mechanism of steel balls in a countershaft gear that block shifts past neutral while the shaft is stationary.
Chain elongation
the increase in length of a chain over a measured number of pitches, expressed as a percentage of the new length; a measure of pin and bushing wear.
Polygon effect
the speed pulsation of a chain as it rises and falls over the flats of a sprocket; larger with fewer sprocket teeth.
Shaft-drive jacking
the rise of the rear of a shaft-drive machine on acceleration, and squat on the overrun, caused by reaction torque at the rear bevel housing.
Paralever
BMW's shaft-drive rear suspension with a torque arm forming a parallelogram with the swingarm, so the bevel housing cannot rotate relative to the frame.
Torque cam
the helical slots and guide pins on a CVT driven pulley that convert drive torque into extra axial force, forcing a lower ratio when the throttle is opened hard.
Kickback
a violent oscillation of the steering (tank-slapper), typically started when the front wheel lands askew after a bump under acceleration.
Wobble
a front-end steering oscillation of about 4–10 Hz, mostly at medium speeds.
Static sag
how far the suspension compresses from full extension under the weight of the machine alone.
Rider sag
how far the suspension compresses from full extension with the rider in riding position; also called race sag.
Stiction
static friction in seals and bushes that stops suspension moving freely at small loads, so sag readings differ when the bike is lifted or pushed to rest.
Wheel rate
the effective spring rate measured at the wheel, about the shock spring rate divided by the square of the motion ratio.
Tangential lacing
spoke lacing in which spokes leave the hub at a tangent and cross one another, so drive and brake torque is carried by spokes pulling on the hub.
Plug-patch
a combined plug and inner patch fitted from inside a removed tubeless tyre: the only permanent tubeless puncture repair.
Static balancing
balancing a wheel on its bearings or an arbor so that the heavy spot settles at the bottom, then adding weight opposite until the wheel stays in any position.
Hydraulic ratio
the ratio of caliper piston area (one side of the disc) to master cylinder piston area, by which line pressure multiplies force.
Self-servo
the effect by which friction drags the leading shoe of a drum brake harder into the drum, increasing braking force.
Rollback
the slight return of a brake caliper piston pulled back by its square-section seal when pressure is released, which keeps the pads just clear of the disc.
Radial mount
a caliper fixing with bolts parallel to the disc radius, loading the bracket in a stiffer direction than an axial mount.
T-CLOCS
the Motorcycle Safety Foundation's pre-ride checklist: tyres and wheels, controls, lights and electrics, oil and fluids, chassis, stands.
PDI (pre-delivery inspection)
the structured assembly, check, adjustment and road test of a new machine before it is handed to the customer.
